glosses: lawful, legal, regulation
правильный, соответствующий
Réglementaire, régulier, conforme à la règle, au règlement.

examples.text: Mit Ernüchterung mussten die Verantwortlichen nämlich feststellen, dass ihr Beteiligungsmodell für die staatliche Regulierungsbehörde Elcom als nicht regelkonform gilt und in der Form nicht mehr fortgeführt werden kann.
examples.translation: En effet, les responsables durent constater avec désillusion que leur modèle de participation est jugé non conforme aux règles par lʼautorité de régulation d’État Elcom et ne peut plus être poursuivi sous cette forme.

examples.text: Berührt man eine Figur, mit der kein legaler Zug möglich ist, dann hat das keine Auswirkungen, man kann einen beliebigen regelkonformen Zug ausführen.
examples.translation: Si l’on touche une figure avec laquelle aucun mouvement réglementaire n’est possible, cela n’a aucun effet ; on pout effectuer n’importe quel mouvement conforme aux règles.

glosses: den Regeln entsprechend

examples.text: Der Querpass war absolut regelkonform.

glosses: Bound by religious rule; belonging to a monastic or religious order (often as opposed to secular).

examples.text: regular clergy, in distinction from the secular clergy
A quarter of a million strong in 1680, the clergy was only half as large in 1789. The unpopular regular clergy were the worst affected.

glosses: Having a constant pattern; showing evenness of form or appearance.
Both equilateral and equiangular; having all sides of the same length, and all (corresponding) angles of the same size
Whose faces are all congruent regular polygons, equally inclined to each other.
Demonstrating a consistent set of rules; showing order, evenness of operation or occurrence.

examples.text: April may be the cruellest month, but I am planning to render it civilised and to take my antibiotics in a regular manner.

glosses: Of a moon or other satellite: following a relatively close and prograde orbit with little inclination or eccentricity.
Well-behaved, orderly; restrained (of a lifestyle etc.).
Happening at constant (especially short) intervals.

examples.text: He made regular visits to go see his mother.

glosses: Following a set or common pattern; according to the normal rules of a given language.

examples.text: "Walked" is the past tense of the regular verb "to walk".

glosses: Having the expected characteristics or appearances; normal, ordinary, standard.

examples.text: “I don’t see how you can write and act such splendid things, Jo. You’re a regular Shakespeare!” exclaimed Beth, who firmly believed that her sisters were gifted with wonderful genius in all things.

For a spell we done pretty well. Then there came a reg'lar terror of a sou'wester same as you don't get one summer in a thousand, and blowed the shanty flat and ripped about half of the weir poles out of the sand.

glosses: Permanently organised; being part of a set professional body of troops.
Having bowel movements or menstrual periods at constant intervals in the expected way.

examples.text: Maintaining a high-fibre diet keeps you regular.
Gulls cawed and wheeled overhead, dropping splatty white cluster bombs on rooftops and pavements. Goodness knows what those gulls eat, but it certainly keeps them regular.

glosses: Exemplary; excellent example of; utter, downright.

examples.text: a regular genius; a regular John Bull
Don't worry, boy. We're gonna set you straight. By tomorrow morning, you'll be a regular Burt Reynolds.

glosses: Having all the parts of the same kind alike in size and shape.

examples.text: a regular flower; a regular sea urchin

glosses: Isometric.
Riding with the left foot forward.
Such that every set in its domain is both outer regular and inner regular.
Noetherian and such that the minimal number of generators of the maximal ideal is equal to the Krull dimension of the ring.
Such that the local ring at every point is regular.
A von Neumann regular: such that every left module (over the given ring) is flat.
Regularly, on a regular basis.

examples.text: 'And if the knowledge wasn'y well come by, why, you might ha' made up for it by coming to church reg'lar.'
Though no minister would visit the Skerburnfoot, or, if he went, departed quicker than he came, the girl Ailie attended regular at the catechising at the mains of Sker.
"There's only twenty men staying in the house regular," said Ahearne, showing him around[.]
"Drain her every thousand, regular. Don't do it myself, o' course; just drop her in at the lubritorium."
"All we've got to do is stick 'em in the bedroom and feed 'em regular."

glosses: A member of the British Army (as opposed to a member of the Territorial Army or Reserve).
A frequent, routine visitor to an establishment.

examples.text: Bartenders usually know their regulars by name.

glosses: A member of the armed forces or police force.
A member of the armed forces or police force.
Synonym of regular serviceman; a soldier in the Singapore Armed Forces who has chosen to work full-time beyond their required length of service in the army.

examples.text: Boss, this is the situation. They were regulars in the army. They’ve left the army and are taxi drivers now. He was a commando and he was a state boxer. They don’t earn much and there’s no end.

glosses: A frequent customer, client or business partner.

examples.text: This gentleman was one of the architect's regulars.

glosses: A coffee with one cream and one sugar.
Anything that is normal or standard.

examples.text: You separate the marbles by color until you have four groups, but then you notice that some of the marbles are regulars, some are shooters, and some are peewees.

glosses: A member of a religious order who has taken the three ordinary vows.
A number for each year, giving, added to the concurrents, the number of the day of the week on which the Paschal full moon falls.
A fixed number for each month serving to ascertain the day of the week, or the age of the moon, on the first day of any month.
Strictly adhering to rules, legal requirements, or official procedures.

examples.text: Given the troubled Bayou State's long history of rogues and demagogues, the most unusual thing about Gov. Jindal may be his record of by-the-book ethics.

glosses: Qui appartient au règlement ; qui est conforme au règlement.

examples.text: D'un côté, vous aviez le taulard, vêtu du droguet réglementaire, chaussé de sabots et tondu à ras. De l'autre, le surveillant, impeccablement sanglé dans son uniforme, casquetté de frais, […].
Il retrace les méandres, les scoumounes qui ont conduit ces grands enfants du malaise collectif à ces cellules réglementaires de 3 × 3 mètres.

glosses: Qualifie un acte émanant du pouvoir exécutif.

examples.text: Les projets d’ordonnance constituent un cas particulier. En effet, il s’agit d’actes de nature réglementaire, jusqu’à leur ratification par le Parlement.

glosses: Variante orthographique de réglementaire.
